messages: ellie: quick design question — for the Create API key form, should we validate inline as people type or wait until submit and show a grouped error summary? leaning inline for quick fixes but worried about noise on long forms. samir: +1 to inline for the small fields (name, email) but for multi-step things maybe summary at the top on submit. avoids interrupting flow. maria: if we go inline, let's be careful with required affordances. asterisks are subtle and missed by screen readers. prefer explicit 'Required' label for the critical fields. kai: accessibility nit: regardless of inline vs summary, make sure we set aria-invalid and focus to the first errored control in JS. also announce the total errors in an aria-live region for screen reader users. ellie: agree on aria-live. thinking about hybrid: inline lightweight errors (single sentence) attached to fields, plus an error summary on submit that groups anything missed. keeps feedback local but still surfaces everything. samir: that hybrid is what many teams use. UX question: tone of microcopy. we have a bunch of different voices — some are terse, some super apologetic. proposal: use direct, action-oriented copy: 'Enter a valid email' instead of 'Sorry, this email appears to be invalid'. maria: +1 on direct language. for destructive actions (delete API key) do we do a full type-to-confirm ('Type DELETE') or a two-step modal with checkbox? which is less friction for power users? kai: type-to-confirm prevents accidental clicks but is a lot of friction. maybe use progressive friction: simple modal for most users, require typed confirmation for org-level or irreversible ops. we should map by risk level. ellie: proposed pattern: 1) low-risk delete -> single-button modal with clear consequence text and primary/secondary buttons 2) high-risk (revokes clients, infra impact) -> typed confirmation. document in the pattern library. uxbot: [deploy-bot] New design token batch deployed for form-error colors — semantic tokens: color-error, color-error-on-surface. samir: UX detail: how do we show required fields? asterisk only, or inline summary that lists "Fields marked required"? maria: asterisk + visually hidden text for screen readers: use required next to the label, instead of relying on title attributes. kai: example snippet that we should adopt in the codebase: ``` Enter a valid email ``` ellie: looks good. also + add role=\"alert\" on the error text when it appears after submit, to ensure it reads. maria: quick microcopy table suggestion for the pattern library (short, medium, long): - inline: "Enter a valid value" - summary: "We found 3 problems. Fix the highlighted fields below." - destructive modal primary: "Delete API key" (red) secondary: "Cancel" samir: I'm concerned about over-using red error states for minor hints. please keep 'hint' styles separate from 'error' styles. ellie: agreed — add a design token set for hint vs error and add visual distinction (lighter text + icon for hint). kai: accessibility checklist for the PR: set aria-invalid, focus-first-error, error-summary anchor links, aria-live or role=\"status\" for inline hints, ensure color contrast for error text meets AA, provide keyboard focus for modals. maria: nit: when we present the error summary at top, make the anchor links use data-qa ids so e2e tests can focus them reliably. ellie: next steps: i'll update the pattern doc with the hybrid pattern, add microcopy suggestions, and create a small PR with the snippet and tokens. owner: @ellie, reviewers: @maria and @kai. target: next sprint. samir: sounds good. tagging design-ops to add to the console patterns page. :+1: ellie: thanks all, will post the draft link when ready."
